title: Add SDLC pipeline support for Jira epics
summary: Plan-phase architecture analysis for #1557 — extend the existing submit_task pipeline so a Jira epic key is a first-class SDLC unit of work. Two new IO sinks (refine→epic Description; plan→child Jira tickets) and one new orchestrator-side credential surface (Won't-Do transitions, which are permanently denylisted from the gateway) are the headline deltas. Refine and plan phases reuse the same draft+HITL surface (.egg-state/drafts/<id>-*.md) and the same contract store. All 12 HITL decisions and 5 feedback Q&A were resolved in refine. Slicing chose Option A (single slice, A+B+C+D+E+F+G, 1 PR — decision-1). Apply-step location chose hybrid (decision-11): in-sandbox apply-epic agent for editJiraIssue / createJiraIssue / createIssueLink / addCommentToJiraIssue; orchestrator-direct only for the transitions verb. Hierarchy uses JiraPolicy.epic_link_field per-site config (decision-2 opt-3). Reassess-trigger override is a single --mode={auto,reassess,fresh} param on submit_task (decision-12 opt-3). Mapping persists as a new epic_apply key on the pipeline artifact (.egg-state/pipelines/<id>.json) per decision-10. All hard prerequisites (#1556, #1924, #1931, #2137) are landed.

in_scope: (A) submit_task epic-input handling: detect Jira issuetype.name == 'Epic' after first get_ticket; route through the epic path. Add --mode={auto,reassess,fresh} param (decision-12 opt-3).

(B) Refine prompt tweak: tell the agent the destination is an epic Description (self-contained problem statement + scope, not ticket-shaped). On HITL approval, an apply-epic agent calls gateway editJiraIssue (wholesale rewrite — decision-9) and records the prior Description fetch+diff guard.

(C) Plan prompt tweak: produce, per node, a fully-formed Jira ticket body (Problem statement / Scope / Acceptance criteria / Out of scope / Cross-links — fixed structure per feedback Q2). Plan parser remains the existing egg_contracts.plan_parser entrypoint; the yaml-tasks appendix gains new fields (existing_key, action: create|edit|consolidate|split|wont_do|untouched, link_edges).

(D) Plan apply step (epic case): two-pass execution by the apply-epic agent through the gateway — pass 1 createJiraIssue + editJiraIssue + addCommentToJiraIssue (consolidation redirects); pass 2 createIssueLink for cross-task edges. Each call carries an idempotency_key derived from plan-node id + commit SHA. Mapping (plan-node → Jira key) written to .egg-state/pipelines/<id>.json under epic_apply.

(E) Orchestrator-direct Jira credentials + Won't-Do transition helper: new shared module (shared/egg_jira_orchestrator/transitions.py or similar) that reads ~/.config/egg/secrets.env via a resolver mirroring gateway/jira_credentials.py (ATLASSIAN_* then JIRA_* fallback per-key); helper POSTs to /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/transitions. Helper invoked only after plan-apply, only for non-in-flight children flagged obsolete. Emits structured audit log (epic_key, child_key, from_status, to_status, principal).

(F) Reassess child discovery + classification + plan diff: two separate JQL searches (parent = <EPIC> ; <epic_link_field> = <EPIC>) merged; classify into to_do / done / in_flight (per decision-4: Done children excluded from prompt; in_flight passed in with do-not-modify-without-confirmation marker). Plan prompt receives the (to_do + in_flight) set with status + open-PR signals attached.

(G) In-flight detection (per decision-8 opt-4 — OR semantics, signal-source logged on HITL gate): three signals — Jira fields.status.name in {In Progress, In Review, Code Review, Blocked, …}; orchestrator pipeline-state with open PR (canonical via _get_pr_info on pipeline_id=<CHILD-KEY>); ticket remoteLinks with github.com/…/pull/ URLs. Per-ticket HITL gate registered for any mutation (edit / consolidate-away / Won't-Do) on an in_flight child; creates that merely depend on an in_flight child apply normally.

(F-bis) Plan apply's consolidation survivor selection (decision-5): agent emits per-consolidation survivor + rationale in the plan draft; operator overrides per-node before plan approval (no heuristic).

(G-bis) PR-link writeback to Jira (feedback Q4): when a child's implement opens a PR (_auto_create_pr at pipelines.py:9430), gateway-add a remoteLink on the child key pointing at the PR URL. Cross-task dependency link types allowlist from {Blocks, Is blocked by, Relates to}, agent-chosen per-edge with rationale (feedback Q3).

(I) Confluence link discovery (decision-7 opt-3): refine sweep gathers Jira remoteLinks + URL-scrape of epic Description and existing-children Descriptions + remoteLinks of linked Jira issues (recursive one level).
out_of_scope: Jira-label-driven state machine (egg-sdlc / egg-awaiting-response) — explicitly deferred by issue's `What this issue is not`.

Implement-phase cross-child coordination/auto-spawn — decision-6 resolved to 'operator decides at the plan approval gate (Stop-after-plan vs Continue-to-implement)'. The implement orchestration for that 'Continue' branch is just today's per-child submit_task path applied to each plan node; no new auto-spawn scheduling logic.
A new gateway get_project_metadata verb to auto-detect parent vs Epic Link per project — decision-2 opt-3 reuses JiraPolicy.epic_link_field. Auto-detect (opt-1) is a future upgrade.
Lifting the JIRA_WRITE_VERBS_DENIED denylist for transitions — off the table by #1556 scope.
Optimistic-concurrency If-Match ETag on edit_issue — v1 uses fetch-and-diff guard only.
Aggregate epic-level PR — issue explicitly resolved per-child-ticket PRs.
Bulk-create Jira endpoint — serialize creates through gateway for v1; revisit if rate-limit pressure justifies adding bulk support (would need gateway change).

key_decisions_consumed.decision-1_slicing: Option A — single slice, A+B+C+D+E+F+G, 1 PR. The architect agrees with this resolution; the reassess code path shares scaffolding with the fresh path (same plan apply, same gateway calls), so splitting them inflates seam cost. All sub-deliverables (A–G) are wired into one PR per the chosen option.
key_decisions_consumed.decision-2_hierarchy_field: Operator-configurable per Jira project — sourced from JiraPolicy.epic_link_field (gateway/jira_policy.py:163–170). The apply step passes this through to create_issue(..., epic_link_field=<configured>). No gateway verb addition needed; reuses the per-site primitive that already exists.
key_decisions_consumed.decision-3_wont_do_gating: Batch on single plan approval — operator sees the obsolete list in the plan draft, approves wholesale. Per-ticket gate exists only for in_flight (decision-8 + the resolved in-flight sub-section).
key_decisions_consumed.decision-4_done_children: Exclude entirely from plan prompt. Diff annotation in plan draft can still note 'Done children left untouched: X, Y, Z' as a one-line audit (does not feed the prompt).
key_decisions_consumed.decision-5_consolidation_survivor: Agent picks per-consolidation with rationale; operator overrides per-node in the plan draft before approval. Survivor selection serialized into the plan draft's yaml-tasks (existing_key field).
key_decisions_consumed.decision-6_implement_trigger: Operator decides at the plan-approval gate: Stop-after-plan vs Continue-to-implement. The Continue branch uses today's sliced implement phase; each child ticket is its own slice in the slice DAG. No submit_task param and no auto-spawn at submit time.
key_decisions_consumed.decision-7_confluence_discovery: Remote links + Description URLs + linked Jira issues' remote links (recursive one level).
key_decisions_consumed.decision-8_in_flight_precedence: OR semantics with signal-source logged on HITL gate. The HITL prompt names which signal fired (status / orch-pipeline / ticket-remotelink).
key_decisions_consumed.decision-9_reassess_refine_output: Wholesale rewrite of epic Description. Apply step still fetch-and-diffs against the version the agent saw, surfacing a divergence HITL if an operator manually edited in the interim.
key_decisions_consumed.decision-10_mapping_persistence: Pipeline artifact (.egg-state/pipelines/<id>.json under a new `epic_apply` key). Survives draft rewrites; matches today's pr_url artifact pattern.
key_decisions_consumed.decision-11_apply_location: Hybrid: in-sandbox apply-epic agent for editJiraIssue / createJiraIssue / createIssueLink / addCommentToJiraIssue (through the gateway, with the gateway audit identity = session token); orchestrator-direct only for transitions (the gateway-blocked verb). Preserves 'agents write through the gateway' symmetry for everything that has a gateway path.
key_decisions_consumed.decision-12_mode_param: Single --mode={auto,reassess,fresh} parameter on submit_task. Default 'auto' preserves today's behavior; explicit overrides bypass detection. New optional MCP param on submit_task signature.
key_decisions_consumed.feedback_q1_orch_creds: Reuse ~/.config/egg/secrets.env (same file gateway/jira_credentials.py reads). Orchestrator-side helper mirrors that resolver pattern in a new shared module — ATLASSIAN_* then JIRA_* fallback per-key. Rotation = same as gateway's. Audit = structured log per transition.
key_decisions_consumed.feedback_q2_ticket_body: Fixed structure: Problem statement / Scope / Acceptance criteria / Out of scope / Cross-links. Section ordering enforced in plan prompt + validated by plan parser (or a thin post-parse validator).
key_decisions_consumed.feedback_q3_link_types: Agent picks per-edge from default allowlist {Blocks, Is blocked by, Relates to}; plan draft surfaces choice + rationale; operator overrides per-edge.
key_decisions_consumed.feedback_q4_pr_writeback: Implement-phase opens PR → gateway adds remoteLink on the child key pointing at the PR URL (uses gateway's addRemoteLink verb if present, otherwise add via the gateway's existing remote-link primitive; verify primitive existence below).

submit_task_handler.new_param_slot: Add `mode: Literal['auto', 'reassess', 'fresh'] = 'auto'` as a sibling of jira_ticket in the MCP schema (around lines 100-105). Validation in the handler body picks the branch after the jira_ticket regex check at 1287-1300.
submit_task_handler.epic_detection: submit_task does NOT fetch ticket content today (no get_ticket call from orchestrator). Two viable patterns: (a) orchestrator-side issuetype probe via the orchestrator GatewayClient (would need a new Jira read shim on GatewayClient, not present today — see gap below); (b) lazy detection inside the refine agent itself (agent calls jira ticket get, switches prompt branch via EGG_PIPELINE_MODE env, writes the mode back to contract). Pattern (b) defers the issuetype probe to the agent and avoids adding a Jira shim to GatewayClient; pattern (a) makes routing deterministic at create_pipeline time. Recommend (a) for cleaner routing — see Architecture Decisions § Issue-Type Detection.

pipeline_model.add_decision_helper: orchestrator/models.py:1016 (in-memory decision tracking; not the contract-store path)
pipeline_model.new_epic_apply_field: Add a typed model `EpicApplyArtifact` (created_keys: dict[str, str] plan_node→jira_key; edited_keys: list[str]; wont_do_keys: list[str]; link_edges: list[LinkEdge]; refine_description_sha256: str; idempotency_seed: str) and slot it onto Pipeline as an Optional field around 982. Persisted in .egg-state/pipelines/<id>.json.

draft_io.naming: Drafts named `<pipeline_id>-analysis.md` / `<pipeline_id>-plan.md`. Pipeline_id for an epic is the epic key (e.g. `KORE-1234`). No changes needed.

phase_transition_path.no_existing_apply_hook: There is NO post-approval 'apply' hook in the codebase today. Decision-11's hybrid model means we add an apply step that runs *after* HITL approval and *before* the phase transition. The cleanest place is a new dispatcher in orchestrator/routes/phases.py that on advance_phase from refine (when pipeline.mode != fresh and epic-detected) spawns an `apply-epic` agent slice for the refine sink, and on advance_phase from plan does the same for the plan sink. The orchestrator-direct transitions helper runs server-side immediately after the apply-epic agent's slice completes.

architecture_overview.headline: Three IO sinks: epic Description (gateway editJiraIssue); child tickets + links + comments (gateway create_issue + create_issue_link + add_comment); Won't-Do transitions (orchestrator-direct POST). One new shared credential module for the orchestrator-direct path. One new pipeline-artifact key (epic_apply) for idempotent re-apply.

component_breakdown.name: submit_task epic-input handling
component_breakdown.delta: Add `mode` MCP param (decision-12). At handler entry, if jira_ticket is set and mode != 'fresh', orchestrator calls a new GatewayClient.get_jira_issuetype(<KEY>) shim (new method on GatewayClient) to probe issuetype.name; if 'Epic' AND children exist (via the two-JQL discovery) AND mode == 'auto', set pipeline.mode = 'reassess'; otherwise pipeline.mode = 'fresh'. The mode lands on the Pipeline model + EGG_PIPELINE_MODE env passed to the sandbox.
new_primitives: GatewayClient.get_jira_issuetype + .jira_search shim (light HTTP wrappers around gateway routes)

component_breakdown.name: Refine prompt + epic-Description sink
component_breakdown.delta: New conditional block keyed off pipeline.mode in {'reassess', 'fresh'} AND epic-detected: prompt frames the analysis as a self-contained epic Description (problem statement + scope), not a refined ticket statement. In reassess mode, prompt is given the existing-children diff (status + open-PR signals attached). On HITL approval (advance_phase refine→plan), a new dispatcher in orchestrator/routes/phases.py spawns an `apply-epic` agent slice that calls gateway editJiraIssue on the epic key with the refine draft body. Apply step fetches the current Description first; if the SHA-256 differs from the snapshot the agent saw (recorded in epic_apply.refine_description_sha256), it registers a divergence-confirmation HITL decision and waits.
new_primitives: apply-epic agent role (sandbox container; uses gateway session token)

component_breakdown.name: Plan prompt + per-node ticket bodies + cross-task DAG
component_breakdown.delta: Plan prompt mandates per-node sections in order: Problem statement / Scope / Acceptance criteria / Out of scope / Cross-links (feedback Q2). Cross-task DAG edges agent-chosen from {Blocks, Is blocked by, Relates to} (feedback Q3). yaml-tasks gain optional fields: existing_key, action (create/edit/consolidate/split/wont_do/untouched), link_edges (list of (target_node_id, link_type, rationale)), in_flight, survivor_rationale. Plan parser change is additive — new fields default to None; existing tests still pass.
new_primitives: yaml-tasks schema extension (existing_key, action, link_edges, in_flight, survivor_rationale)

component_breakdown.name: Plan apply step — two-pass create/edit/link/comment
component_breakdown.delta: On advance_phase plan→implement, the dispatcher spawns the apply-epic agent slice with the plan draft + epic_apply mapping context. Agent: (Pass 1) for each yaml-task with action == create OR split, call gateway create_issue(epic_link or parent set from JiraPolicy.epic_link_field); for action == edit OR consolidate (survivor), call edit_issue; for action == consolidate (non-survivor), call add_comment with the redirect message; record every (plan_node_id, jira_key) in epic_apply.created_keys / .edited_keys. (Pass 2) for each link_edge, call create_issue_link with idempotency_key = sha256(plan_node_id + target + commit_sha). All gateway calls carry idempotency_key (gateway already supports per-call idempotency). After both passes, the orchestrator-direct transition helper runs server-side for every yaml-task with action == wont_do that is NOT marked in_flight; in_flight wont_do entries spawn per-ticket HITL gates first.

component_breakdown.name: Orchestrator-direct Won't-Do transitions
component_breakdown.delta: credentials.py mirrors gateway/jira_credentials.py: reads ~/.config/egg/secrets.env (or EGG_SECRETS_PATH); ATLASSIAN_USERNAME / ATLASSIAN_API_TOKEN with JIRA_* fallback; raises JiraOrchestratorCredentialsUnavailable if any of base_url / username / token is missing (orchestrator caller logs WARN + falls back to recording the wont_do entries as 'requires_manual_transition: true' in epic_apply rather than failing the whole apply). transitions.py: thin POST to /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/transitions/ using a transition_id resolved via GET /transitions (workflow-state-name → id, with a Won't Do allowlist). Emits structured audit log per transition: epic_key, child_key, from_status, to_status, principal=ATLASSIAN_USERNAME, transition_id, http_status.
new_primitives: Audit log line format (new structured logger event_type=jira_orchestrator_transition)
Won't-Do workflow-state-name allowlist (config; defaults to {'Won\'t Do', 'Wont Do', 'Won\'t do'})

component_breakdown.name: Reassess child discovery + classification
files: orchestrator-side discovery helper in routes/pipelines.py (or new orchestrator/jira_reassess.py)
component_breakdown.delta: Two-pass JQL via GatewayClient.jira_search shim: (a) `parent = <EPIC>`; (b) `<JiraPolicy.epic_link_field> = <EPIC>` (skipped when the configured field is 'parent' — tautology). Both queries tolerate HTTP 400 (custom-field-missing) and merge results. For each child: fetch get_ticket with fields=['status', 'issuetype', 'parent', 'description', 'remoteLinks'] (single batched GET per child — Jira batched GET is not free; for >20 children, plan-time decision on whether to pre-batch or per-child). Classify into {to_do, done, in_flight} via decision-8 OR logic; record signal_source. Feed (to_do + in_flight) into the plan prompt; record (done) only as a plan-draft footer audit note (decision-4).
new_primitives: ChildClassification dataclass (key, status, signal_source, in_flight: bool)

component_breakdown.name: In-flight detection + per-ticket HITL gate
files: orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py (HITL gate registration in apply runner)
component_breakdown.delta: Signal 1: status.name in IN_FLIGHT_STATUSES allowlist (configurable; defaults to {'In Progress', 'In Review', 'Code Review', 'Blocked'}). Signal 2: GET ~ orchestrator/.egg-state/pipelines/<CHILD-KEY>.json — if phases.pr.artifacts.pr_url present AND PR is open (use _get_pr_info to validate), in_flight=True. Signal 3: scan ticket remoteLinks for github.com/.../pull/<n> URLs (via gateway). OR all three; record `in_flight_signal_source` = which fired. Apply runner: before calling edit_issue / add_comment(redirect)/transition on any in_flight child, register an mcp__sdlc__register_open_question per-ticket with the proposed mutation + signal source; pause apply until resolution.
new_primitives: Per-ticket HITL gate registration helper (reuses mcp__sdlc__register_open_question)

component_breakdown.name: PR-link writeback to Jira (feedback Q4)
component_breakdown.delta: After _auto_create_pr opens a PR for a child pipeline whose pipeline_id is a Jira key, fire a gateway addRemoteLink call (or post a comment if the addRemoteLink primitive is not available — see Gaps) targeting the child key with the PR URL + title. Idempotent via remoteLink globalId derived from pipeline_id.
new_primitives: Optional gateway addRemoteLink verb (primitive-existence check pending — see Gaps)

component_breakdown.name: Confluence link discovery during refine (decision-7 opt-3)
component_breakdown.delta: Refine prompt enumerates the three sources: (i) gateway remoteLinks on the epic key; (ii) URL-scrape the epic Description body for Confluence URLs (atlassian.net/wiki/spaces); (iii) for each linked Jira issue (via issueLinks), fetch its remoteLinks too (recursive one level). All gateway-mediated; no new orchestrator code. Refine agent uses confluence_client.get_page / search_cql as needed.

architecture_overview.sub_slice_structure_within_option_A:
Single-slice Option-A still benefits from a logical sub-ordering within the implement phase. Suggested sub-task DAG (task_planner consumes this):

1. **Foundation**: Pipeline.mode field + EGG_PIPELINE_MODE env + EpicApplyArtifact pydantic model + epic_apply pipeline-artifact persistence. No behavior change yet.
2. **GatewayClient shims**: jira_search, get_jira_issue, get_jira_issuetype (only Jira read shims) on orchestrator GatewayClient. Unit-tested against a stub gateway.
3. **submit_task wiring**: mode param + issuetype detection + reassess child discovery + classification. Routes pipeline.mode at create_pipeline time.
4. **Prompts**: refine + plan epic-branch fragments in _build_phase_prompt; plan_parser yaml-tasks extension.
5. **Apply-epic agent**: new agent role; prompt template; sandbox-side gateway-mediated apply (create/edit/link/comment).
6. **Orchestrator-direct transitions**: shared/egg_jira_orchestrator credentials + transitions module; structured audit log; Won't-Do executor.
7. **In-flight HITL gate**: signal aggregation + per-ticket gate registration in the apply runner.
8. **PR-link writeback**: _auto_create_pr post-hook (depends on gateway primitive existence).
9. **Tests + docs**: integration tests for end-to-end fresh-epic and reassess paths; CLAUDE.md + docs/guides update.

These sub-tasks share a single PR (decision-1) but the task_planner should still produce the DAG so reviewers can audit sequentially.
trust_boundaries: GATEWAY-MEDIATED WRITES: editJiraIssue (epic Description + child edits), createJiraIssue (new children + splits), createIssueLink (cross-task edges), addCommentToJiraIssue (consolidation redirects), addRemoteLink (PR writeback, if primitive present). Execution context: in-sandbox-agent (apply-epic agent). Gateway audit identity = session token. JiraPolicy.epic_link_field per-site config applies.

ORCHESTRATOR-DIRECT (no gateway): Won't-Do transitions only. Execution context: trusted-CI-runner (orchestrator). Credentials read from ~/.config/egg/secrets.env via the new shared/egg_jira_orchestrator/credentials.py resolver. NEVER reused for create/edit/link/comment — gateway path is canonical for those. The new credential reader must NOT import from gateway/* (process-boundary symmetry); shared/* is the right home.

ORCHESTRATOR-DIRECT READS (light): the orchestrator already calls the gateway for git/session ops via GatewayClient; adding three light Jira read shims (issuetype probe, search, get_issue) is a small extension that keeps the trust boundary intact (orchestrator → gateway HTTP → Atlassian). The orchestrator does NOT add a direct Atlassian path for reads.

HITL GATE BYPASS — NON-BYPASSABLE: the in_flight per-ticket gate is enforced server-side in the apply runner (orchestrator), not in the agent prompt. The agent records the proposed mutation; the apply runner refuses to invoke edit/comment/transition on an in_flight child until the per-ticket HITL is resolved. This is the only way to prevent a buggy agent prompt from bypassing the gate.

ZERO-CREDENTIAL SANDBOX INVARIANT: the apply-epic agent runs in the sandbox container; it inherits only the gateway session token (no Jira creds). The new shared/egg_jira_orchestrator module runs orchestrator-side only — its secrets file is NEVER mounted into the sandbox.

purpose_vs_execution_context_axes.principle: Per #2594, the two axes are orthogonal. A primitive can be unit-test-only or production; it can be invoked from in-sandbox-agent or from trusted-CI-runner. Below are the cells that matter for this issue.
in_sandbox_agent_production_writes: gateway create_issue / edit_issue / add_comment / create_issue_link (apply-epic agent path)
in_sandbox_agent_production_reads: gateway get_ticket / search / confluence_client.* (refine agent path)
trusted_ci_runner_production_reads: orchestrator-side gateway-shim Jira reads (issuetype probe + reassess discovery at create_pipeline time)
unit_test_only: test fixtures for ChildClassifier, InFlightDetector, EpicApplyArtifact serialization — all live under tests/ and never deployed

architecture_decisions.title: Issue-Type Detection — orchestrator-side at create_pipeline time, not lazy in the refine agent
architecture_decisions.decision: Add three Jira read shims on the orchestrator's GatewayClient (get_jira_issuetype, jira_search, get_jira_issue) so submit_task can probe issuetype.name immediately. Why: routing the pipeline through the fresh vs reassess vs ticket branches at create_pipeline time keeps the rest of the orchestrator deterministic. Lazy detection inside the refine agent would push branch-routing into prompt-conditional logic + later env-var write-back, which is much harder to reason about and harder to test.
architecture_decisions.trade_off: Adds three light shim methods to GatewayClient (~30 LOC each). Worth it for determinism.

architecture_decisions.title: Apply Step Execution — Decision-11 Hybrid implemented as dispatcher hook on advance_phase
architecture_decisions.decision: Refine apply (epic Description) fires from the orchestrator phase-advance dispatcher (on refine→plan); plan apply (children + links + comments) fires from the same dispatcher (on plan→implement). Each apply is implemented as a one-off `apply-epic` agent slice in the sandbox, with the gateway session token providing audit identity. The orchestrator-direct transition helper runs server-side immediately after the apply-epic agent's plan-phase slice completes. Why: keeps the gateway audit story uniform with today's 'agents write through the gateway' pattern; confines the orchestrator-direct credential surface to its single justified caller (transitions).
architecture_decisions.trade_off: Two extra agent invocations per epic pipeline. Acceptable for v1; can be inlined later if cost matters.

architecture_decisions.title: Idempotency — per-call idempotency_key + epic_apply mapping
architecture_decisions.decision: Every create_issue / edit_issue / create_issue_link / add_comment call carries an idempotency_key derived from sha256(plan_node_id + action + commit_sha[:12]). epic_apply.created_keys / .edited_keys / .link_edges / .wont_do_keys serve as the durable resume marker. On re-apply, the runner checks each entry against the mapping before issuing the gateway call. The gateway already supports the idempotency_key parameter on these verbs (jira_client.py).
architecture_decisions.trade_off: Slightly chatty epic_apply state; mitigated by Pydantic serialization + the existing pipeline-snapshot persistence path.

architecture_decisions.title: Two-Pass Apply — Create/Edit before Link
architecture_decisions.decision: Pass 1: all create/edit/comment calls. Pass 2: all create_issue_link calls. Why: every link needs both endpoints to exist. Won't-Do transitions can fire in Pass 1 (transitions don't depend on links) but only AFTER any consolidation-survivor edit and after per-ticket in_flight HITL resolves.
architecture_decisions.trade_off: Marginal latency cost; correctness gain is decisive.

architecture_decisions.title: Concurrent-Edit Guard on Epic Description — fetch-and-diff (v1)
architecture_decisions.decision: Apply-epic agent fetches the current Description before calling edit_issue. Computes sha256 of the fetched body. If it diverges from the snapshot the refine agent saw (recorded as epic_apply.refine_description_sha256), registers an mcp__sdlc__register_open_question with the diff and pauses apply until operator resolves. Why: the gateway does not support optimistic-concurrency (If-Match ETag) on edit_issue today; fetch-and-diff is the minimum bar against silent overwrites of manual edits.
architecture_decisions.trade_off: Two round-trips per refine apply (fetch + edit). Acceptable; optimistic-concurrency is a future follow-up.

architecture_decisions.title: Orchestrator Jira Credential Module Location — shared/egg_jira_orchestrator/
architecture_decisions.decision: New shared/egg_jira_orchestrator/credentials.py + transitions.py mirroring gateway/jira_credentials.py's resolver pattern but in a separate package importable by orchestrator/* only. Reads ~/.config/egg/secrets.env (or EGG_SECRETS_PATH). Does NOT import from gateway/*. Why: process-boundary symmetry — the orchestrator and gateway are separate processes; the orchestrator gets its own credential reader that happens to read the same file.
architecture_decisions.trade_off: Modest code duplication with gateway/jira_credentials.py. Worth it for the trust-boundary clarity.

architecture_decisions.title: In-Flight Gate Enforcement — Server-Side, Not Prompt-Side
architecture_decisions.decision: The apply-epic agent records the proposed mutation per in_flight child. The orchestrator-side apply runner checks in_flight at apply time (status / open-PR can change between plan approval and apply) and refuses to invoke any mutating call on an in_flight child until the per-ticket HITL gate is resolved. The agent prompt frames the gate informationally; enforcement is server-side. Why: a buggy or prompt-injected agent must not be able to bypass the gate.
architecture_decisions.trade_off: Requires the apply runner to re-fetch status before each mutation. Acceptable cost; mitigated by batching status fetches per pipeline run.

architecture_decisions.title: Plan Mapping Persistence — Pipeline Artifact, Not Plan Draft
architecture_decisions.decision: epic_apply lives on .egg-state/pipelines/<id>.json (Pipeline pydantic field), not inline yaml-frontmatter in the plan draft (which was the architect-recommended fallback). The operator-resolved decision-10 stands; matches today's pr_url pattern; survives plan-draft rewrites.

architecture_decisions.title: Reassess Discovery — Two-Query JQL, Tolerate-400, Merge
architecture_decisions.decision: Single disjunctive JQL of the form `parent = <K> OR "Epic Link" = <K>` returns HTTP 400 when one custom field is missing on the searched project. Use two separate queries, tolerate per-query 400s, merge results. The second query (`<epic_link_field> = <EPIC>`) is skipped as a tautology when JiraPolicy.epic_link_field == 'parent'.
architecture_decisions.trade_off: Two queries per epic; rate-limit cost is trivial.

architecture_decisions.title: Done-Children Surfacing — Footer Audit Note in Plan Draft
architecture_decisions.decision: Decision-4 excludes Done children from the plan prompt. They are surfaced only as a one-line plan-draft footer ('Done children left untouched: X, Y, Z') so the operator sees the full reassessment picture without inviting agent re-planning.
architecture_decisions.trade_off: None — operator-resolved decision; footer note is mechanical.

open_questions_for_plan_phase.question: Does the gateway expose an addRemoteLink verb on Jira tickets today? Feedback Q4 (PR-link writeback) needs it. Verify by reading gateway/jira_client.py for 'remote', 'addRemoteLink', or grep gateway/routes for /jira/.../remotelink. If absent: (a) extend the gateway with this verb (small) OR (b) use the gateway's execute_raw passthrough OR (c) fall back to add_comment with the PR URL. Plan should land (a) if missing; (c) is the no-fallback fallback.

Should the orchestrator's GatewayClient.jira_search shim cap max_results, or stream/paginate? An epic with 200 children could hit single-page limits. Recommend: cap at 100 per call + cursor-paginate via gateway's existing pagination support.

Where exactly does the apply-epic agent slice get spawned from? Today's slice scheduler lives in orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py around _create_slice_pipeline. Need to confirm whether 'one-off agent slice' = a real new sliced pipeline or a synchronous in-process agent invocation. Recommend: a synchronous agent invocation (NOT a new pipeline) — it shares the parent pipeline_id + branch + state and is short-lived.

How does the apply-epic agent get the gateway session token? Today's sandbox containers receive a session token via GatewayClient.register_session. The apply-epic agent needs the same plumbing — confirm that register_session can be invoked from a non-implement-phase context, or whether a separate session-token plumbing is needed for refine/plan apply runs.

Does the orchestrator-direct transition helper need a dedicated principal (e.g. egg-orchestrator-bot@…)? Or does it reuse ATLASSIAN_USERNAME? Feedback Q1 says reuse, but operators may want a distinct identity for transitions so the audit trail is clearer. Plan can land 'reuse ATLASSIAN_USERNAME by default; allow EGG_ORCH_JIRA_USERNAME override' to give both paths.

Reassess child discovery + classification adds latency at submit_task time (issuetype probe + two JQL queries + one get_ticket per child). For an epic with 50 children, that's ~52 gateway calls. Plan should decide: (a) do this synchronously at submit_task (blocks the caller); (b) defer to refine-phase entry and surface progress; (c) split into a 'discovery' microphase. Recommend (a) for v1 — the caller is the operator's host session which can wait a few seconds. Re-evaluate if the latency materializes as a complaint.

risks_for_risk_analyst: R1 — Orchestrator-direct credential surface is novel; mistakes here are credential-leak risks. Mitigation: shared/egg_jira_orchestrator never imported by sandbox-bound code; tests assert the import boundary.

R2 — Won't-Do transition could fire on the wrong child (e.g. agent misclassifies). Mitigation: server-side in_flight re-check at apply time; transition allowlist constrained to Won't-Do-equivalent states; structured audit log per transition.
R3 — Bulk-create rate-limit pressure at apply time (epic with 30+ children). Mitigation: serialize gateway calls; reuse gateway's existing rate-limit retry; defer bulk-create endpoint to a follow-up.
R4 — Concurrent-edit silent overwrite of operator's epic Description edit. Mitigation: ad-5 fetch-and-diff + divergence HITL.
R5 — In-flight gate bypass via buggy agent prompt. Mitigation: ad-7 server-side enforcement, not prompt-side.

R6 — Plan-node → key mapping corruption (manual edits to .egg-state/pipelines/<id>.json). Mitigation: Pydantic schema validation on load; re-apply path is idempotent so a wiped mapping just re-creates (with new keys — potential duplicate-ticket risk, see R7).

R7 — Mapping wipe + re-apply duplicates Jira tickets. Mitigation: idempotency_key derived from plan_node_id + commit_sha gives the gateway a dedupe handle for re-creates within the same plan commit; cross-commit dedupe requires the mapping (so the operational guidance is 'never wipe the mapping').

R8 — Per-site Epic Link field misconfiguration causes silent hierarchy break (children created without parent). Mitigation: apply step verifies the configured field is set on the create_issue response; fails loud if missing.

R9 — Custom link types like 'Blocks' / 'Is blocked by' may not exist in every project. Mitigation: fail-soft (log + skip + record in epic_apply.link_edges with applied_at=None); operator sees the report in the plan-apply summary.
R10 — Cross-task DAG cycles in agent output. Mitigation: plan parser validates the link_edges form a DAG (topological-sort check); cyclic plan rejected with a NACK message.

R11 — Reassess discovery latency on huge epics (200+ children) blocks submit_task. Mitigation: max_results cap + cursor pagination + a configurable discovery cap (default 200). Beyond cap: error with a clear operator message.
R12 — JiraPolicy.epic_link_field operator misconfig (typo). Mitigation: gateway already allowlists via _VALID_EPIC_LINK_FIELDS — invalid values rejected at gateway startup.

complexity_assessment.rationale: Touches MCP tool surface, two phase prompts, a brand-new apply step pattern, a new credential surface, in-flight detection across three signals, per-ticket HITL gating, idempotent mapping persistence, and trust-boundary changes across orchestrator/gateway/sandbox. Mitigated by all hard prerequisites being landed and by the resolved 12 decisions narrowing the design space significantly.
